source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Set BMC power policy to always-on.
2. System does AC off and check LAN is workable after AC on.
3. Set BMC policy to always-off and check step 2 without power on system

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. BMC LAN should be workable after AC on, no matter system power on or not.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- not runnable by agent: this case cycles physical AC power to the system (AC off then AC on) after setting the BMC power-on policy, and checks the BMC LAN works after AC-on whether the system powers on or not. The AC connector is a physical mains switch only a person at the machine can operate; agent cannot cut AC remotely.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator sets the BMC power policy (always-on / always-off) from the BMC, physically cycles AC off/on, and confirms the BMC LAN responds after AC-on in both polities; agent can only confirm BMC reachability (ping/lan print) after the operator cycles AC.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO based on assumed physical-only AC action.

original_test_intent: For always-on and always-off host power policies, remove and restore AC and verify the BMC LAN recovers independently of the resulting host power state.
original_method: Set each policy, perform an AC loss/restore using the project-approved method, then poll BMC identity, network and host state.
manual_activity: Engineer approves the policy/AC plan and power topology. If the project provides an approved addressable AC controller, the complete core can run automatically; the source does not require a human cable pull.
required_inputs: AC outlet/feed-to-SUT map and approved controller
Off/on dwell and BMC reconnect timeout
Stable storage state and recovery path
safety_requirements: Do not infer manual cable pulling or substitute software reboot for AC loss.
Verify exact power target and protect in-use data.
Perform one approved unchanged sequence with no automatic retry.
Safety-stop on power/network/host anomaly and preserve first failure.
agent_execution_scope: After approval, set each policy, operate the approved AC controller, poll BMC LAN/identity and host state, collect SEL/network evidence and restore policy.
engineer_actions: Perform AC manually only if the project lacks an approved automatable controller.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its claim that AC must be physically human-operated is not stated by this row and is not generalized from Seq 182.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Prefer the approved PA Manager/project AC controller; do not use BMC power-off or reboot as AC-loss substitutes.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both policies, true AC off/on, LAN independence, script and 10/10 minutes remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Snapshot state, apply each policy, perform true AC loss/restore via mapped approved controller, time BMC network recovery and verify expected host state, then restore policy.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact power-feed/controller and BMC policy implementation.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform AC recovery policy and approved lab power-control SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds target mapping, timing and recovery without changing true-AC coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Preserves AC loss rather than substituting software power.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: AC loss interrupts the host and may affect data.

project_override_considerations: If execution is manually switched, record that method; Seq 182's manual-only decision is case-specific and is not applied here. No project may claim AC coverage from a software reboot.
expected_evidence: BMC LAN identity/reconnect and host state per policy

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently requires true AC loss/restoration; it does not prescribe a physical cable pull or contradict the two policy phases.

blocked_analysis.analysis: An approved AC controller is a readiness input. The core is fully automatable where provided; absence alone does not make it permanently blocked or manual-only.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its unsupported global physical-only assumption.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Reclassifies MANUAL ONLY to FULLY AUTOMATABLE capability while preserving true-AC coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Applies the explicit Seq 182 case-specific boundary.

review_improvement: Preserves genuine AC-loss semantics while allowing an approved project controller and separating capability from site tooling.
independent_technical_reasoning: Nothing in this row mandates a hand-pulled cable. A mapped AC controller can reproduce the electrical loss and capture recovery deterministically; BMC power commands cannot.

source_provenance.history: Round02 exact variant and ED-32/Seq-182 case-specific decision
